classification.difficultyReason: Recognise the perfect-square condition, form a quadratic equation in the parameter using the discriminant, and solve it.

content.prompt: Find the values of $\ell$ that will make the quadratic $y=(\ell+6)x^2-2\ell x+3$ a perfect square.

answer.short:
$\ell=6$ or $\ell=-3$.

A perfect-square quadratic has discriminant zero.
answer.worked:
For a perfect square, $\Delta=0$.
$$\begin{align*}\Delta&=(-2\ell)^2-4(\ell+6)(3)\\\Delta&=4\ell^2-12\ell-72.\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}4\ell^2-12\ell-72&=0\\\ell^2-3\ell-18&=0\\(\ell-6)(\ell+3)&=0\\\ell&=6\text{ or }-3.\end{align*}$$
Both values give perfect squares:
$$\begin{align*}\ell=6:\quad y&=12x^2-12x+3=3(2x-1)^2,\\\ell=-3:\quad y&=3x^2+6x+3=3(x+1)^2.\end{align*}$$
